Newton's first law of motion: An object at rest stays at rest; an object in motion stays in motion at the same speed in the same direction — unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force. This is the law of inertia. Practical: a satellite in orbit stays in orbit without thrust because space has no friction. A ball rolls indefinitely on a frictionless surface. Every mechanical system depends on overcoming inertia to start and exploiting it to maintain motion.
Newton's second law of motion: Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma). A larger force produces greater acceleration; a larger mass requires more force for the same acceleration. Practical: a 10kg object requires 98 Newtons to hold against gravity (10 × 9.8 m/s2). Engine power requirements scale with vehicle mass. Structural loads scale with mass and deceleration forces — critical for building design and vehicle safety.
Newton's third law of motion: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. When you push on a wall, the wall pushes back on you with equal force. Rocket propulsion: exhaust gas pushed backward, rocket pushed forward. Practical: all structural connections must handle reaction forces equal to applied loads. Recoil in firearms. Jet propulsion. Sailing against the wind using the same principle through angle of attack.
first law of thermodynamics: Energy cannot be created or destroyed — only converted from one form to another. Total energy of an isolated system is constant. Practical: a coal fire converts chemical energy to heat; a steam engine converts heat to mechanical work; both obey energy conservation. Efficiency = useful energy out / total energy in. No engine can produce more energy than it consumes (perpetual motion is impossible).
second law of thermodynamics: Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold, never cold to hot without work input. Entropy (disorder) of an isolated system always increases or stays the same. Practical: a refrigerator requires work input to move heat from cold interior to warm room. All real engines are less than 100% efficient because some energy becomes low-grade heat. Useful work can be extracted only from temperature differences. Maximum theoretical efficiency (Carnot): 1 - (Tc/Th) where temperatures are in Kelvin.
Ohm's law electricity: Voltage = Current × Resistance (V = I × R). Practical: a 12V battery through 6 ohm resistance produces 2 amperes current. Power = Voltage × Current (P = VI) = I2R. ELECTRICAL SAFETY: 50mA through heart region is lethal; skin resistance varies 1000-100,000 ohms wet vs dry. CIRCUIT BASICS: series resistors add (R = R1+R2); parallel resistors: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2. Larger wire gauge handles more current without overheating — always match wire to load.
photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy → C6H12O6 (glucose) + 6O2. Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs red (680nm) and blue (450nm) light; reflects green. LIGHT REACTIONS: split water, release oxygen, produce ATP and NADPH. CALVIN CYCLE (dark reactions): uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into glucose. Rate limited by: light intensity, CO2 concentration, temperature, water availability. Basis of all food chains on Earth. C4 plants (corn, sugarcane) more efficient in hot/bright conditions than C3 plants.
cellular respiration: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + ATP (energy). GLYCOLYSIS: glucose split into 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP, no oxygen required. KREBS CYCLE: pyruvate fully oxidized, produces CO2, electron carriers. ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN: 32-34 ATP produced per glucose using oxygen as final electron acceptor. ANAEROBIC (no oxygen): lactic acid fermentation (muscle) or ethanol fermentation (yeast) — only 2 ATP. Fats yield 2x more ATP per gram than carbohydrates. Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell.
germ theory of disease: Specific microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites) cause specific diseases — not miasma or imbalanced humors. Koch's postulates (1884): 1) microorganism found in all cases; 2) isolated from diseased host; 3) causes disease when introduced to healthy host; 4) re-isolated from newly diseased host. PRACTICAL: hand washing, sterilization, clean water, sanitation, vaccines, and antibiotics all derive from germ theory. Understanding pathogen transmission routes (airborne, fecal-oral, contact, vector) determines prevention strategies.
water cycle hydrological: EVAPORATION: solar energy converts liquid water to vapor (ocean = 85% of atmospheric moisture). TRANSPIRATION: plants release water vapor through stomata (contributes 10% of atmospheric moisture). CONDENSATION: water vapor cools, forms droplets around condensation nuclei (dust, pollen) — forms clouds. PRECIPITATION: droplets coalesce and fall as rain/snow. RUNOFF: flows to rivers and groundwater recharge. GROUNDWATER: 30% of all fresh water; recharge rates from centuries to millennia. The cycle purifies water through evaporation (salts and most pathogens left behind).
nitrogen cycle: 79% of atmosphere is N2 — biologically inert until fixed. NITROGEN FIXATION: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules convert N2 to ammonia (NH3); free-living bacteria; lightning. NITRIFICATION: bacteria convert NH3 to nitrite then nitrate — plant-available form. ASSIMILATION: plants absorb nitrate, build proteins. AMMONIFICATION: decomposers break down organic matter back to ammonia. DENITRIFICATION: other bacteria convert nitrate back to N2 completing the cycle. PRACTICAL: crop rotation with legumes, compost, and manure are all nitrogen management strategies.
lever principle mechanics: Load × Load arm = Effort × Effort arm (conservation of energy). THREE CLASSES: Class 1 (fulcrum between load and effort — seesaw, scissors): can multiply force or distance. Class 2 (load between fulcrum and effort — wheelbarrow, nutcracker): always multiplies force. Class 3 (effort between fulcrum and load — tweezers, fishing rod): multiplies distance/speed, reduces force. MECHANICAL ADVANTAGE = Load arm / Effort arm. A 3m crowbar with fulcrum 30cm from load has MA of 9 — multiplies your force 9x. Foundation of all simple machines.
pulley systems: SINGLE FIXED PULLEY: changes direction of force, no mechanical advantage. SINGLE MOVABLE PULLEY: 2:1 mechanical advantage (haul 100kg with 50kg force). BLOCK AND TACKLE (multiple pulleys): MA equals number of rope segments supporting movable block. 4-pulley system: haul 100kg with 25kg force (MA=4). FRICTION LOSSES: each pulley adds approximately 10% friction loss. PRACTICAL: rigging rescue systems, building construction, well systems. Z-PULLEY (mountaineering): improvised high MA from two pulleys and prussik — 3:1 minimum, often 6:1 with redirect.
electricity generation principles: ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION (Faraday's Law): moving conductor in magnetic field generates voltage. All generators work on this principle. EMF = -N × d(flux)/dt. GENERATOR COMPONENTS: permanent magnets or electromagnets, rotating coil (or rotating magnets around fixed coil), commutator (DC) or slip rings (AC). POWER OUTPUT = voltage × current. PRACTICAL SMALL-SCALE: water wheel with permanent magnet alternator, wind turbine, bicycle generator. Efficiency 60-85% for well-designed systems. Frequency = RPM × pole pairs / 60.
solar energy basics: PHOTOVOLTAIC EFFECT: photons knock electrons free in semiconductor (silicon), creating current. Solar cell efficiency: commercial silicon 15-22%; best lab cells 47%. SOLAR CONSTANT: 1361 W/m2 at Earth's orbit; ground level ~1000 W/m2 maximum. INSOLATION: average daily solar energy by latitude — equator 5-6 kWh/m2/day; mid-latitudes 3-4; poles 1-2. PANEL SIZING: 1kW system at 80% efficiency in 5-peak-sun hours = 4 kWh/day. BATTERY STORAGE: Ah capacity × voltage = Wh; size for 2-3 days autonomy. Tilt angle = latitude for fixed mounts.
water wheel power: OVERSHOT (water falls on top): most efficient 60-85%; requires head (height) of water. UNDERSHOT (water flows under): 15-30% efficient; only stream current needed, no head. BREASTSHOT (mid-wheel): 50-60% efficient. POWER CALCULATION: P = ρ × g × Q × h × efficiency, where ρ=1000kg/m3 water, g=9.8m/s2, Q=flow rate m3/s, h=head in meters. A 1m3/s stream with 3m head at 70% efficiency = 20.6 kW. Historically powered grain mills, sawmills, trip hammers for metalworking.
fermentation chemistry: ALCOHOLIC FERMENTATION (yeast): C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH (ethanol) + 2CO2. Yeast active 18-35C; alcohol above 12-14% kills yeast. LACTIC ACID FERMENTATION: C6H12O6 → 2CH3CHOHCOOH (lactic acid); Lactobacillus, no oxygen, acidifies to pH 3.5-4.5 — preserves food, inhibits pathogens. ACETIC ACID (vinegar): ethanol + oxygen → acetic acid, via Acetobacter at surface. All three processes release energy from glucose without burning it. Historical importance: bread, cheese, beer, wine, yogurt, vinegar are all fermentation products.
metallurgy basics iron and steel: IRON ORE REDUCTION: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2 in blast furnace at 1200-1500C. Coke (purified coal) provides carbon monoxide reducing agent. PIG IRON: 3-4% carbon — brittle, not useful as-is. WROUGHT IRON: carbon below 0.1%, worked by repeated hammering at red heat (removes carbon) — tough and ductile. STEEL: 0.2-2% carbon — strong and ductile. HEAT TREATMENT: quench (rapid cooling) hardens steel; tempering (reheating lower temperature) reduces brittleness. CHARCOAL SMELTING: traditional method requires 10kg charcoal per 1kg iron produced.
concrete and lime construction: HYDRAULIC LIME: heat limestone (CaCO3) above 900C → quicklime (CaO) + CO2. Add water: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) — exothermic reaction, 65C. Mix with sand and water for mortar or plaster. CONCRETE: cement (hydraulic lime or Portland) + sand + aggregate + water. ROMAN CONCRETE (pozzolanic): volcanic ash + lime + seawater — sets underwater, stronger than modern concrete after 2000 years. WATER-TO-CEMENT RATIO: 0.4-0.5 optimal; more water = weaker concrete. Curing: keep moist 28 days for full strength development.
glass making: SILICA + SODIUM CARBONATE + LIME: heat to 1400-1500C. Silica (SiO2) from clean quartz sand; sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) lowers melting point to workable range. SODA-LIME GLASS (window glass): 74% SiO2 + 13% Na2O + 11% CaO. POTASH GLASS (historical, from wood ash): potassium replaces sodium — harder, clearer, higher melting point. WORKING TEMPERATURE: 1000-1100C for blowing/shaping. ANNEALING: cool slowly in controlled kiln to relieve internal stress — rapid cooling causes fracture. Wood ash provides both lime and potash — historically glass was made near forests.
soap making saponification: COLD PROCESS: fat or oil + strong alkali → soap + glycerol. LYE: wood ash in water leaches potassium hydroxide (soft soap); calcium hydroxide from bone ash or limestone makes harder soap. MODERN: sodium hydroxide (NaOH) for hard soap; potassium hydroxide (KOH) for soft/liquid soap. SAPONIFICATION VALUE: different fats require different lye amounts — tallow 140g NaOH/kg, olive oil 134g/kg, coconut oil 190g/kg. PROCESS: heat fat to 50C, add lye solution slowly at same temperature, mix to trace, pour into molds, cure 4-6 weeks. Glycerol byproduct is moisturizing.
distillation principles: SEPARATION: liquid mixture heated, more volatile component evaporates first, vapor condensed and collected separately. BOILING POINTS: water 100C; ethanol 78.4C; methanol 64.7C (poisonous, never for drinking). SIMPLE DISTILLATION: one evaporation-condensation step. FRACTIONAL DISTILLATION: multiple plates or packing increase effective distillation steps — petroleum refining separates gasoline (30-200C), kerosene (150-250C), diesel (200-350C). SOLAR STILL: solar energy evaporates salt/polluted water, condenses on cool surface, drips to collection trough — 0.5-1L/m2/day.
electricity storage batteries: LEAD-ACID (most common): lead plates in sulfuric acid, 2V per cell, 6 cells for 12V. Charge cycles: 200-500 for starter battery; 1000+ for deep-cycle. LITHIUM ION: 3.6V per cell, 4x energy density of lead-acid, 2000+ cycles but expensive. CAPACITY: amp-hours (Ah) × voltage = watt-hours (Wh). A 100Ah 12V battery stores 1200Wh = 1.2kWh. BATTERY BANK SIZING: calculate daily consumption in Wh, multiply by days of autonomy, divide by battery voltage, multiply by 1.2 safety factor, multiply by 2 for 50% depth of discharge limit for longevity.
plant cell anatomy: CELL WALL (plant-specific): rigid cellulose structure provides shape and support — absent in animal cells. CHLOROPLAST (plant-specific): site of photosynthesis; contains chlorophyll; has own DNA (endosymbiotic origin from ancient cyanobacteria). VACUOLE: large central vacuole stores water, maintains turgor pressure (wilting = loss of turgor). NUCLEUS: contains DNA, directs protein synthesis. MITOCHONDRIA: cellular respiration, ATP production. CELL MEMBRANE: phospholipid bilayer, selectively permeable. PLASMODESMATA: channels connecting adjacent cells for communication and transport.
genetics heredity basics: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid): double helix of 4 bases (A-T, G-C base pairs). GENE: sequence of DNA coding for one protein. CHROMOSOME: DNA packaged with proteins; humans have 46 (23 pairs). ALLELES: alternative versions of a gene. DOMINANT/RECESSIVE: dominant allele expresses when present; recessive only expresses in homozygous state. MENDELIAN RATIOS: two heterozygous parents for one trait produce 3:1 dominant:recessive ratio in offspring. MUTATION: change in DNA sequence — source of genetic variation and evolution. PRACTICAL: understanding genetics enables selective breeding for crop and livestock improvement.
chemistry pH scale: pH = -log10[H+] concentration. RANGE: 0-14. pH 7 = neutral (pure water). pH below 7 = acidic (H+ ions dominate). pH above 7 = alkaline/basic (OH- ions dominate). LOGARITHMIC: pH 5 is 10x more acidic than pH 6; pH 4 is 100x more acidic. AGRICULTURAL IMPORTANCE: most crops grow best at pH 6.0-7.0; blueberries prefer pH 4.5-5.5; asparagus tolerates pH 6.5-7.5. WATER CHEMISTRY: safe drinking water pH 6.5-8.5. ACID RAIN: pH 4.2-4.4. Buffer solutions resist pH change. Test with universal indicator strips or red cabbage juice (natural pH indicator).
speed of light and electromagnetic spect: Speed of light in vacuum: 299,792,458 m/s (approximately 3x10^8 m/s). ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM (low to high frequency): radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light (400-700nm wavelength), ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. All are electromagnetic radiation traveling at speed c. PRACTICAL: radio waves carry communications; microwaves carry radar and WiFi; infrared = heat radiation; visible = sight; UV causes sunburn and sterilizes water (UV-C 254nm kills 99.9% of microorganisms); X-rays penetrate soft tissue for imaging; gamma rays from nuclear reactions — most penetrating and dangerous.
principles of flight aerodynamics: LIFT: generated by difference in pressure above (low) and below (high) wing due to airfoil shape and angle of attack. BERNOULLI: faster-moving air above wing has lower pressure. ANGLE OF ATTACK: increased angle increases lift but above stall angle (~15-18 degrees) lift collapses. DRAG: friction + form drag — minimize with streamlining. THRUST: propeller or jet engine provides forward force. WEIGHT: gravity downward. LEVEL FLIGHT: Lift = Weight; Thrust = Drag. GLIDE RATIO: unpowered aircraft descends 1m for every X meters forward; albatross 22:1; hang glider 12:1; parachute 1:1.
nuclear energy basics: FISSION: heavy nucleus (U-235 or Pu-239) absorbs neutron, splits into lighter nuclei + 2-3 neutrons + energy. Chain reaction: each fission releases neutrons that cause more fissions. CRITICAL MASS: minimum fissile material for self-sustaining chain reaction — U-235 approximately 52kg spherical (reduced to 15kg with reflector). REACTOR CONTROL: neutron-absorbing control rods (boron, cadmium) slow or stop chain reaction. ENERGY DENSITY: 1kg U-235 = 24,000 MWh thermal energy vs 1kg coal = 8 kWh. FUSION: hydrogen isotopes fuse to form helium, releases more energy per unit mass than fission — powers the Sun, not yet achieved commercially.
tectonic plates geology: Earth's lithosphere divided into approximately 15 major tectonic plates moving 2-10cm per year, driven by convection in mantle. DIVERGENT BOUNDARIES: plates separate, magma fills gap — mid-ocean ridges, East African Rift Valley. CONVERGENT BOUNDARIES: plates collide — oceanic subducts under continental (creating volcanoes and trenches), two continents collide (creating mountains like Himalayas). TRANSFORM BOUNDARIES: plates slide past each other — San Andreas Fault. EARTHQUAKES: concentrated at plate boundaries; magnitude logarithmic (each integer = 32x energy increase). Volcanoes: predominantly at convergent and divergent boundaries.
climate zones classification: KOPPEN CLASSIFICATION: A=Tropical (no cold season); B=Arid (evaporation exceeds precipitation); C=Temperate (mild winters); D=Continental (cold winters); E=Polar. FACTORS: latitude (solar angle), altitude (lapse rate 6.5C/1000m), ocean proximity (moderating effect), ocean currents (Gulf Stream warms Europe 5-10C above latitude average), prevailing winds, topography (rain shadow effect). AGRICULTURAL IMPLICATIONS: frost-free days, growing degree days, annual precipitation, and seasonality determine viable crops. Climate zones shifting poleward approximately 5-6km/year due to current warming trend.
electromagnetic induction Faraday: A changing magnetic field induces an electromotive force (EMF) in a conductor. EMF = -N × dΦ/dt (N = number of coil turns, Φ = magnetic flux). LENZ'S LAW: induced current direction opposes the change that caused it. TRANSFORMER: AC current in primary coil creates changing magnetic field, induces AC in secondary coil. Voltage ratio = turns ratio: 10 turns primary, 100 turns secondary = 10x voltage step-up. GENERATOR: mechanical rotation of coil in magnetic field produces AC electricity — basis of all electrical generation. MOTOR: reverse of generator — current in magnetic field produces mechanical force.
